text:
Quinn Hughes told The Athletic's Michael Russo he's playing the best hockey of his career, and the numbers back him. He has 32 points in 23 games, a 12-game point streak of his own (NHL Stats counts him and Kirill Kaprizov as only the 11th forward and defenseman pair with simultaneous 12-game streaks), and he's playing 29 minutes a night lately, up more than two from his season average. Minnesota takes 57.6% of the expected goals at five on five with him on, almost 10 points better than without him.

Evolving-Hockey had him as the most valuable defenseman in the league last season, 4.9 wins above replacement, first among 215. The new part is the shot: seven goals already, on 4.0 expected, shooting 12% after 4% last year. That will cool. The passing won't; he was in the 99th percentile among defensemen for primary shot assists in Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking.

The trade chatter of last season has flipped too. The headlines now say he and the Wild are a pairing for a Cup push, not a rental.
